title: Typhoon Dujuan Makes Landfall in SE China
main_content:
Typhoon Dujuan made landfall in southeastern China Tuesday causing strong winds and heavy rains just hours after sweeping through parts of Taiwan.

Three people were killed in Taiwan after the typhoon struck the island nation, according to the country’s Central Emergency Operation Center. More than 300 others were injured, many hit by flying debris or involved in traffic accidents.

Across the island severe winds uprooted trees, damaged vehicles and cut power to nearly a million people.

Schools and businesses remain closed in Taiwan Tuesday while railways slowly resumed service.

The center of the storm passed Taiwan early Tuesday and moved on to China’s eastern Fujian province.

The storm first hit the coastal city of Putian at around 8:50 a.m. with winds of up to 33 meters per second, according to China’s official Xinhua news agency. No deaths or injuries have been reported.

Flights, ferry and train services were suspended throughout the province. Xinhua reports workers are trying to restore power to more than 600,000 homes.

questions.question: What did typhoon Dujuan cause in southeastern China?
options: Widespread flooding and loss of agricultural produce
Strong winds and heavy rains leading to suspended services
A significant decrease in tourism and travel disruptions
Numerous casualties and severe infrastructure damage
questions.answer: Strong winds and heavy rains leading to suspended services

questions.question: How were people injured during the typhoon?
options: By falling into large bodies of water
From being hit by flying debris or involved in traffic accidents
Through direct contact with the storm surge
By electrical injuries due to downed power lines
questions.answer: From being hit by flying debris or involved in traffic accidents

questions.question: What were the effects of the strong winds?
options: Only minor disruptions with no significant consequences
Severe winds uprooted trees, damaged vehicles, and cut power
Enhancements to local infrastructure and emergency response
A rise in popularity for outdoor recreational activities
questions.answer: Severe winds uprooted trees, damaged vehicles, and cut power
